notes: Summary: Large ecommerce personalization platform evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency ranking and chat-support augmentation.
Primary ask: explicit throughput guarantees for committed pool plus defined burst behaviour. Want min tokens/sec per tenant and concurrency caps to protect multi-tenant microservices.
Current thinking: reserve 8x H100-equivalent GPUs initially (predicting ~240M tokens/min sustained across models), with headroom for short bursts up to 2x for <=60s.
Latency SLO: 95th pctile <= 150ms token-latency for chat (context <=1024), 99th pctile <= 400ms for reranking jobs (batch size 8).
Cost sensitivity: mid-high; will trade higher committed spend for firm throughput SLA and predictable p50 latency. Wants clear overage pricing and burst caps.
Routing/fallback: prefer primary model family on H100 reserved pool, automatic fallback to quantized variant on cheaper GPU if capacity constrained. Needs control plane flags for routing policy.
Security/compliance: requires VPC deployment with customer-managed KMS, SSO for admin console, and audit logs forwarded to Splunk. Data residency US-only for training-derived embeddings.
Quote from CTO on 2026-02-18 call: "We need a contractual minimum tokens/sec so our UX teams can guarantee response times during peak shopping events."
POC notes: 2-week POC scheduled for 2026-03-08; objective: validate sustained throughput profile and burst behaviour during simulated Black Friday traffic (10x baseline).

Measurement plan: Redwood to provide token/sec telemetry per route, GPU utilization, and per-model p95/p99 latency timelines. Orch Axiom will run synthetic load via internal harness and share results.

Negotiation points called out by procurement: define concurrency cap semantics (per-tenant vs global), burst billing unit (per-minute vs per-10s), and remediation credits for SLA misses (service credits ladder).
Legal requested: sample Dedicated contract with explicit burst policy language and guaranteed minimum tokens/sec. Wants third-party audit clause and incident RCA timeline (72h).

Internal Redwood ask: confirm autoscaling cooldown windows and emergency burst throttles; propose two burst tiers: soft-burst (seconds, no charge until X) and hard-burst (chargeable, limited by concurrency cap).
Decision criteria: Meets latency SLOs under sustained load; clear, predictable cost model; contractual SLA language accepted by legal; timeline alignment with Q3 feature rollout.
